comment: One row for each rule of part 1 of the leak rule of D17.20 in the emptiness pass
(src/fort/owner/prover.ft): the obligation of each exit kind, the scope of a named local at a
`return`, the facts and the bits that prove an exit, and the work limit. Then one row for each
rule of the leak report (src/fort/owner/report.ft) and of the option --leak-report
(src/fort/driver.ft). The first stage runs the cases over FIR text and over lowered fort source
(test/fort/owner/prover_test.ft), with one case for each exit kind: the closing brace, `return`,
`break`, `continue` and an exit into an abort block, and the report
(test/fort/owner/report_test.ft). The second runs the driver test, which holds that no build
changes its verdict. The third runs the oracle test, which prints a false accept for each row
that makes the pass prove an exit that a run leaks at. The table runs in the Linux VM with the
debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the product compiler, whose driver
The first round of a run can read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first row is one that

mutations.what: a `dead` marker in an abort block keeps its obligation
a `dead` marker has no obligation: the closing brace, the `break` and the `continue` lose theirs
a parameter has no obligation at a `return`
a temporary has no obligation at a `return`
a named local whose scope did not end has no obligation at a `return`
a `dead` ends no scope, so each named local has an obligation at each `return` after its store
a store into a named local starts no scope
an address of a named local starts no scope

mutations.what: the scope of a named local has not ended at the entry
the exit of a scratch local holds whatever its bit says
the exit of a local with a fact holds whatever its fact says
the walk of an exit skips the statement right before it
past the work limit each exit holds
the leak work counts no fact of an exit
an exit that the pass does not prove is an error of the build
